findings.body:
**Target:** R3/T-4/T-7 and the per-leaf acceptance matrix
**Issue:** The live registry currently has 67 leaves including query (66 shared), with different guarded/unguarded entries and command-owned validators. The spec gives a global option list but no row per leaf mapping cardinality, value/domain/path semantics, owner, and exact argv outcomes.
**Required change:** Add the required live-registry-derived per-leaf inventory and acceptance rows, or explicitly make a generated artifact/test output the normative record.
**Why blocking:** Tests can omit leaves such as run recover-draft-execution or run filter-task-review, or assign validation to the wrong owner, while still satisfying the current prose.
findings.evidence: The immutable Spec snapshot requires R3/T-4/T-7 to cover the live per-leaf inventory, but it does not define the per-leaf rows or make a generated report normative. The blocking finding remains applicable; authorize only text edits to the named requirement and task implementation notes.

findings.body:
**Target:** R1/R2 and T-1; src/lib/dispatcher.js parseEntryInput
**Issue:** The requirements make alias a canonical option field, but do not state whether aliases are accepted argv forms. parseEntryInput currently ignores args.aliases even though src/lib/cli.js supports aliases, so an alias could be displayed and compared while remaining unparseable.
**Required change:** Specify alias admission and normalization; either restrict aliases to the existing implicit help pair or require alias projection through parseEntryInput/parseArgs with exact argv tests.
**Why blocking:** Parser/help parity and group intersection tests have no determinable expected behavior, and accepting aliases would otherwise require an unstated dispatcher contract change.
findings.evidence: The immutable Spec snapshot mentions alias metadata in R1/R2/T-1 but does not state whether aliases are admitted and normalized by the existing parser owner. The blocking contract gap remains applicable; authorize only text edits to the named requirement and task implementation notes.

findings.body:
**Target:** T-6/R6 and the common-help Acceptance Criteria
**Issue:** sennel plugin and sennel plugin find are core CommandDefinition entries. Plugin-contributed commands are instead loaded through loadPluginRegistry and addressed as sennel <contributed-command> --help. No fixture manifest, command name, or setup is specified for the stated fixture-plugin coverage.
**Required change:** Name the fixture manifest and contributed command used by the test, or reclassify these cases as core plugin-manager help and add a real plugin-contributed command case.
**Why blocking:** The acceptance can pass without exercising the plugin metadata normalization/lazy-import path that the requirement claims to preserve.
findings.evidence: The immutable Spec snapshot names core plugin-manager help cases but does not identify the fixture manifest, contributed command, or setup needed to exercise loadPluginRegistry metadata. The blocking coverage gap remains applicable; authorize only text edits to R6 and T-6 prose.
